answer: One defence is a stake-and-reputation ledger. A new agent must lock a deposit and earn trust gradually through verified work, so creating many fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Like a pearl that forms slowly layer by layer, reputation accrues over time and cannot be rushed. A lantern of audit trails lets peers inspect each agent's history, while a prism of checks - work quality, stake size, and peer endorsements - splits one claim into several verifiable signals. An attacker must fund, age, and maintain many credible identities at once, raising the cost above the gain.
